vehicle.ural.description: The Ural-4320 is a Russian 6x6 off-road truck for cargo, personnel and trailers. It was developed at the Ural Automotive Plant and is also used as a platform for systems such as the BM-21 Grad.
vehicle.btr80a.description: The BTR-80A is an amphibious 8x8 Soviet armoured personnel carrier introduced in 1985. Its 8x8 drive and amphibious hull allow it to operate on roads, rough ground and water.
vehicle.btr_3.description: The BTR-3 is a Ukrainian 8x8 wheeled infantry fighting vehicle. The design combines a welded hull with a remote or manned turret and is exported to several operators.
vehicle.btr_4.description: The BTR-4 Bucephalus is an amphibious Ukrainian 8x8 infantry fighting vehicle. It was designed by the Kharkiv Morozov Design Bureau and has seen service in Ukraine and Iraq.
vehicle.tigr.description: The Tigr is a Russian 4x4 high-mobility armoured vehicle family. The vehicle is used for troop transport, reconnaissance and command duties.
vehicle.pantsir_s1.description: The Pantsir-S1 is a Russian self-propelled air-defence system combining missiles and guns. A typical system vehicle carries a search radar, tracking radar, 12 missiles and two 30 mm autocannons.
vehicle.varta.description: The Varta is a Ukrainian 4x4 mine-resistant armoured vehicle for protected transport. Its protected monocoque hull and blast-resistant design are intended for operations in high-threat areas.
vehicle.varta_ptrk.description: The Varta PTRK is an anti-tank guided-missile variant of the Varta. The missile carrier adds a guided anti-armour launcher while retaining the protected 4x4 chassis.
vehicle.humvee_mk19.description: The HMMWV is an American family of light 4x4 military utility vehicles. The family replaced many light utility vehicles in US service and was widely used in the Gulf War and later conflicts.
vehicle.fmtv.description: The FMTV is a family of US military trucks sharing a common chassis. The family includes light and medium trucks, including cargo, recovery and launcher carriers.
vehicle.stryker.description: The Stryker M1128 was a wheeled direct-fire vehicle based on the Stryker chassis. It was intended to provide a rapidly deployable gun system for Stryker brigade combat teams.
vehicle.stryker_m1296.description: The Stryker M1296 Dragoon is an upgraded 8x8 infantry carrier with a 30 mm turret. The Dragoon was developed to increase the firepower of Stryker infantry units while retaining strategic mobility.
vehicle.m142_himars.description: The M142 HIMARS is a light US multiple rocket launcher on an FMTV chassis. One launcher pod carries either six GMLRS rockets or one ATACMS missile.
vehicle.centauro.description: The Centauro is an Italian 8x8 wheeled tank destroyer with a high-velocity gun. The vehicle was developed for reconnaissance and mobile anti-tank missions and uses an armoured 8x8 chassis.
vehicle.toyota.description: The Toyota Hilux is a Japanese pickup often adapted as a light military technical vehicle. The Hilux uses a ladder frame and is known for simple maintenance and durability in difficult terrain.
vehicle.bushmaster.description: The Bushmaster is an Australian 4x4 protected mobility vehicle for infantry transport. The vehicle uses a V-shaped hull and a large protected cabin, with variants for command, ambulance and engineering roles.
vehicle.t64.description: The T-64 is a Soviet main battle tank introduced in the 1960s with composite armour and an autoloaded 125 mm gun. Its compact layout and three-person crew were enabled by the automatic loader, an influential feature in later Soviet designs.
vehicle.t72_b3m.description: The T-72B3M is a modernised Russian T-72 with upgraded protection, fire control and mobility. The B3M upgrade typically includes a thermal sight, reactive armour and improved communications.
vehicle.t90a.description: The T-90A is a Russian third-generation main battle tank derived from the T-72. The tank combines composite armour with explosive reactive armour and a computerised fire-control system.
vehicle.t90_m.description: The T-90M is a modernised Russian T-90 with improved armour, turret and electronics. The Proryv standard adds a new turret, Relikt reactive armour and a modern digital fire-control suite.
vehicle.t90_pror_2022.description: The T-90M Proryv is a Russian tank modernisation with a redesigned turret and enhanced protection. It is associated with the Proryv modernisation programme and uses the 2A46M-5 125 mm smoothbore gun.
vehicle.t90_pror_2024.description: The T-90M Proryv is a Russian tank modernisation with a redesigned turret and enhanced protection. The configuration represents a later Proryv production standard with updated protection and battlefield equipment.
vehicle.oplot.description: The BM Oplot is a Ukrainian main battle tank developed from the T-84 family. The design retains the T-80-derived layout and uses a 125 mm autoloaded gun with Ukrainian fire-control equipment.
vehicle.terminator.description: The BMPT Terminator is a Russian armoured vehicle designed to support tanks in urban combat. Its armament is intended to engage infantry, light vehicles and positions that are difficult for tank guns to suppress.
vehicle.2c3m.description: The 2S3 Akatsiya is a Soviet self-propelled 152.4 mm howitzer that entered service in 1971. The vehicle is built on a tracked chassis and carries its ammunition and crew inside an enclosed fighting compartment.
vehicle.bmp_2.description: The BMP-2 is an amphibious Soviet infantry fighting vehicle introduced in the 1980s. The BMP-2 carries an infantry squad and provides cannon, machine-gun and anti-tank missile support.
vehicle.bmp_2_bakhcha.description: The BMP-2 Bakhcha is a BMP-2-based vehicle fitted with the Bakhcha combat module. The Bakhcha module normally combines a 100 mm gun-launcher, a 30 mm autocannon and a machine gun.
vehicle.bmp_2m.description: The BMP-2M is a modernised BMP-2 with upgraded sights and guided weapons. The upgrade is intended to improve target acquisition and the ability to defeat armoured vehicles at longer range.
vehicle.bmp_3.description: The BMP-3 is a Soviet and Russian amphibious infantry fighting vehicle succeeding the BMP-1 and BMP-2. Its unusual armament combines a 100 mm gun-launcher with a coaxial 30 mm autocannon.
vehicle.brm.description: The BRM-3K is a Russian tracked reconnaissance vehicle based on the BMP-3 chassis. The reconnaissance vehicle adds observation and communication equipment while retaining the BMP-3 mobility.
vehicle.bmpt_3k.description: The BMPT-3K is a tank-support fighting vehicle in the Russian BMPT family. The BMPT concept uses multiple automatic weapons and guided missiles to cover tanks against close threats.
vehicle.chryzantema.description: The 9K123 Khrizantema-S is a Russian self-propelled anti-tank guided-missile system. The system can use radar or laser guidance and is designed to attack tanks, fortifications and low-flying helicopters.
vehicle.sosna.description: The Sosna is a Russian short-range air-defence system using radar and laser-guided missiles. The launcher is mounted on a tracked chassis and is intended to protect manoeuvring units from aircraft and precision weapons.
vehicle.m60.description: The M60 is an American second-generation main battle tank widely used during the Cold War. The M60 introduced a 105 mm gun and remained a major US and allied tank until the arrival of the M1 Abrams.
vehicle.bradley.description: The M3A3 Bradley is an American tracked cavalry fighting vehicle. The vehicle carries scouts and is armed with a 25 mm Bushmaster cannon and TOW missiles.
vehicle.m1a1.description: The M1A1 Abrams is an American main battle tank armed with a 120 mm M256 gun. The Abrams uses a gas-turbine engine, separate ammunition storage and layered composite armour.
vehicle.m1a1_ukr.description: The M1A1 Abrams Ukraine is a Ukrainian-operated version of the American M1A1. The Ukrainian vehicles are supplied from US stocks and retain the M1A1 configuration and 120 mm armament.
vehicle.m1a2.description: The M1A2 Abrams is an American third-generation tank with advanced fire control and composite armour. The commander independent thermal viewer and digital systems improve target detection and engagement.
vehicle.m1a2_sep.description: The M1A2 SEP V2 is an Abrams upgrade with improved sensors, armour and digital systems. The SEP V2 incorporates improved thermal sights, armour packages and networking for digital battle management.
vehicle.leopard_2a4.description: The Leopard 2A4 is a German third-generation tank armed with a Rheinmetall 120 mm gun. The 2A4 has a four-person crew, a rear-mounted power pack and a stabilised main gun.
vehicle.leopard_2a7v.description: The Leopard 2A7V is a modernised German Leopard 2 with improved protection and electronics. The A7V programme improves mine protection, crew ergonomics, thermal imaging and digital connectivity.
vehicle.challenger.description: The Challenger 2 is a British third-generation tank protected by Chobham armour. Its rifled L30A1 gun and heavily protected turret reflect the British emphasis on long-range gunnery and survivability.
vehicle.puma.description: The Puma is a German infantry fighting vehicle designed to replace the Marder. The Puma uses modular armour and a remote turret, allowing protection to be adjusted for mission requirements.
vehicle.ajax.description: Ajax is a British family of tracked armoured fighting vehicles derived from the ASCOD platform. The family includes reconnaissance, command and recovery variants sharing a common tracked platform.
vehicle.mi_8.description: The Mil Mi-8 is a Soviet medium twin-turbine helicopter used mainly for transport. The airframe can carry troops or cargo and has been adapted for command, rescue and armed missions.
vehicle.mi8_amtsh.description: The Mi-8AMTSh is an armed transport variant of the Mi-8 family. The AMTSh adds armour, a powered loading ramp and weapon pylons for battlefield transport.
vehicle.mi8_mtv3.description: The Mi-8MTV-3 is an improved Mi-8 transport helicopter variant. The MTV series introduced a more powerful drivetrain and improved high-altitude performance.
vehicle.mi17_a.description: The Mi-17A is an export military transport helicopter in the Mi-8/17 family. The Mi-17 family is exported widely and can carry troops, cargo or external loads.
vehicle.mi17_n.description: The Mi-17N is a military transport and gunship variant in the Mi-8/17 family. Armed versions can carry rockets, gun pods and guided weapons on external pylons.
vehicle.mi_24.description: The Mil Mi-24 is a Soviet attack helicopter and limited-capacity troop transport. The armoured cockpit and stub wings allow it to combine troop lift with sustained attack missions.
vehicle.mi_28.description: The Mil Mi-28 is a Soviet-designed all-weather attack helicopter specialised for anti-armour missions. The helicopter has a heavily armoured cockpit, a nose-mounted cannon and stub-wing weapon stations.
vehicle.uh60.description: The UH-60 Black Hawk is an American twin-engine medium-lift military utility helicopter. The Black Hawk is used for assault transport, medical evacuation, special operations and utility missions.
vehicle.uh60mod.description: The UH-60 Mod is a modified configuration of the American UH-60 Black Hawk. The modified configuration can adapt the Black Hawk airframe for additional weapons or mission equipment.
vehicle.ah_64.description: The AH-64 Apache is an American tandem-seat attack helicopter with a 30 mm chain gun. The Apache uses a mast-mounted target sensor and redundant systems to operate in day, night and poor weather.
vehicle.cobra.description: The AH-1Z Viper is an American twin-engine attack helicopter developed from the AH-1W. The Viper uses a four-blade rotor, modern targeting sensors and Hellfire or other guided weapons.
vehicle.nh_90.description: The NH90 is a European twin-engine multi-role military helicopter with fly-by-wire controls. The TTH transport model and NFH naval model share a common airframe and digital avionics.
vehicle.su25.description: The Su-25 Frogfoot is a Soviet subsonic twin-engine aircraft designed for close air support. The aircraft is built around a protected cockpit and redundant systems for low-level battlefield operations.
vehicle.tu22m3.description: The Tu-22M3 is a Soviet supersonic variable-sweep long-range bomber. Variable-sweep wings allow the bomber to combine high-speed flight with long-range cruise performance.
vehicle.f_16.description: The F-16 Fighting Falcon is an American single-engine supersonic multirole fighter. The lightweight airframe, relaxed stability and fly-by-wire controls give the fighter high agility.
vehicle.zu23.description: The ZU-23-2 is a Soviet towed twin-barrel 23 mm anti-aircraft autocannon. The mount is manually aimed and can be towed or installed on trucks and other vehicles.
vehicle.d30.description: The D-30 is a Soviet 122 mm towed howitzer introduced in the 1960s. Its distinctive three-arm trail carriage gives the howitzer a wide traverse without moving the trails.
vehicle.ags_30.description: The AGS-30 is a Russian automatic 30 mm grenade launcher. The launcher is belt-fed and designed to provide sustained indirect or direct grenade fire.
vehicle.tow.description: The BGM-71 TOW is an American wire-guided anti-tank missile widely used on vehicles and helicopters. The operator keeps the sight on the target while the guidance system steers the missile through the wire link.
vehicle.kornet.description: The 9M133 Kornet is a Russian man-portable anti-tank guided missile introduced in 1998. The missile uses laser-beam riding guidance and is available in vehicle-mounted and portable configurations.
